question: Can the instruments be trusted?
rule: Latency analyser (E004): on synthetic loopbacks with known delay, every burst detected and the mean error within 0.05 ms in all cells with SNR of 20 dB or more; the 20.0 ms verdict right at 19.90 and 20.10 ms; the Calibrator callback logic within 1 sample; noise only gives all bursts missed. Crackle detector (E005): recall 0.95 or better for burst amplitude 0.05 and above in every synthetic cell; zero false bursts in 30 clean synthetic captures; random-start bursts give phase concentration R below 0.10 at P = 144. Hardware control (E006): on shared and MME at 48000/256, 5 of 5 runs per path with all 6 bursts detected, xruns 0, peak between -30 and -3 dBFS; spread of the 5 run medians 1.0 ms or less on at least one path and 3.0 ms or less on both; the unplugged-cable run reports NO SIGNAL. PASS = E004, E005 and E006 all pass: set Instrument trust to trusted (E004 and E006 validate the latency instrument, E005 the crackle detector; a pass of only E004 and E006 allows stage 1 numbers to be read but the study field stays untrusted until E005 passes). FAIL = any rule broken: the instrument is fixed by a new task and a new calibration card, and no measure result counts. INCONCLUSIVE = a value between the pass rule and the fail limit of its card: more runs or a finer card.

question: What is the lowest real round trip and does any path reach 20 ms?
rule: Per cell (path, block) from 5 runs of latency_lab with --repeats 1: usable = all 5 runs status OK, 6 of 6 bursts detected, xruns 0, within-run max minus min 1.0 ms or less, spread of the 5 run medians 1.0 ms or less. A cell reaches the goal when it is usable, every one of the 5 run medians is 20.0 ms or less, and mean of the run medians + 3 x max(SD of run medians, 0.05 ms) is 20.0 ms or less. PASS = at least one cell reaches the goal: H005 latency half supported; stage 2 starts at the usable cell with the lowest median RTT and at every goal-reaching cell. FAIL = no usable cell has all 5 run medians at or below 20.0 ms in E007 and E008: the 20 ms goal is refuted for the tested paths and blocks (report the lowest usable RTT) and the plan weighs other hardware or driver options. INCONCLUSIVE = the best usable cell has some run medians at or below 20.0 ms and some above, or its margin rule fails: 10 more runs in that cell before any decision. Also reported (no pass rule): lowest usable RTT with min / median / max, the RTT-versus-block line for H008, shared / MME RTT for H006.

question: Is there a clean setting at the fastest path found?
rule: At each goal-reaching cell from G002 (or at the lowest usable cell if none reaches 20 ms): Lab tone captures of 20 s (1 kHz level 0.3, output capture on, ANALYZE only after unmount) each judged clean when tone error is -55 dB or better, 0 bursts, damaged-window share (windows of 100 ms with at least one burst) under 1 %, no all-zero input blocks and underflows 0. Owner goal tier A = 3 of 3 clean captures after 3 RTT calibrations at or below 20 ms; claim tier B (reliably clean) = 30 of 30 clean captures, failure bound about 10 % (3/n); 10 of 10 gives only about 30 %. PASS (goal met, owner rule) = tier A at one cell; PASS (strong claim) = tier B. FAIL = at least 3 damaged captures in the first 6 at every goal-reaching cell. INCONCLUSIVE = in between: more captures, or the H007 / H004 one-factor cards. Experiments of this stage are written in a later R-PLAN after G002 decides; H007, H002 and H004 are the candidate cards.
